content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question regarding [product_name]. I need to synchronize two drives for an overhead conveyor that is approximately 500 meters long. My approach is to send the same analog voltage to both drives for synchronization. For error detection, two proximity sensors are installed on the sprockets of each drive; I plan to count the pulses to confirm both drives are synchronized and that the chain is intact. The conveyor speeds can be set to five different levels using a switch.
Hello [user_name], Your question is interesting. Could you please clarify whether the two motors are intended to drive a single conveyor belt? Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user expressed uncertainty about whether [product_name] can synchronize two drives using analog voltage and verify this synchronization with proximity sensors. There is a lack of clarity around [product_name]'s ability to count pulses and detect errors to confirm the integrity of the conveyor chain, especially when multiple speed settings are involved. This scenario highlights possible limitations or ambiguities in using [product_name] for drive synchronization and error detection with analog inputs and sensor feedback.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to effectively synchronize two drives through analog voltage and accurately detect issues like chain breakage by counting sensor pulses. They are looking for confirmation about the suitability of [product_name] for these requirements and may need guidance on how to implement this solution.
